chunks: And it was narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Yūnus that his father wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام:
asking him about the fur and the khuff: I wear it and pray in it, while I do not know whether it is properly slaughtered.
So he wrote: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الْفَرْوِ: fur garment or pelt worn as clothing
key_terms.ذَكِيٌّ: properly slaughtered according to the sacred law
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in fur or leather footwear if one does not know whether it came from a properly slaughtered animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about praying in fur or leather footwear when one does not know whether the animal was properly slaughtered. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام replies that there is no harm in it, indicating permissibility in the absence of known impurity or prohibition.
